key_insight: The paper shows that white-box probes can reliably detect deception and sabotage in advanced LLM agents, even in frontier-style monitoring settings. By training on the largest deception dataset to date and aggregating signals across many layers and tokens, the authors achieve very strong detection performance.
problem_solved: How to monitor powerful LLM agents for deceptive behavior and sabotage when harmful intent may be hidden and not directly verbalized.
method: Collected the largest deception dataset to date for training white-box probes.
Introduced a new probe architecture that aggregates information across multiple layers and tokens.
Evaluated the approach in SHADE-Arena, comparing against a strong text-monitoring baseline.
impact: This matters because it suggests scalable monitoring tools can detect hidden deception in advanced AI systems before harmful behavior causes damage. For practitioners, it offers a practical path toward safer deployment of agentic models with stronger oversight.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing deception data collection, probe training, and detection output
Layer-stack graphic illustrating signal aggregation across model layers and tokens
Bar chart comparing AUC performance against the Opus 5.5 text-monitoring baseline
Alert icon or monitoring dashboard visual representing sabotage/deception detection
paper_title: Caught in the Act: Probes Effectively Detect Sabotage and Catch Unverbalized Deception
paper_authors: Oskar J. Hollinsworth, Alex F. Spies, Tigist Diriba, Adam Gleave, Chris Cundy
